clues.clue: DOT is the city agency in charge of these: streets, traffic signals, bike lanes, and the Staten Island Ferry.
clues.reveal: Transportation. The Department of Transportation (DOT) manages streets, signals, bike lanes, and the ferry.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Transportation

clues.clue: DSNY, famous for its plows and 'New York's Strongest,' handles this essential service.
clues.reveal: Sanitation. The Department of Sanitation (DSNY) collects trash and recycling and clears snow.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Sanitation

clues.clue: HPD is the agency that enforces the housing code and finances affordable units; it stands for Housing Preservation and this.
clues.reveal: Development. HPD, the Department of Housing Preservation and Development, enforces the housing code and funds affordable housing.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Housing Preservation and Development

clues.clue: This agency, the DOB, reviews construction plans and issues the permits and certificates of occupancy.
clues.reveal: Buildings. The Department of Buildings (DOB) reviews plans, inspects construction, and issues permits.
clues.src_title: New York City Department of Buildings

clues.clue: City Planning, the DCP, manages zoning and runs this seven-month public land use review process by its acronym.
clues.reveal: ULURP. The Uniform Land Use Review Procedure, managed by the Department of City Planning, is the public process for major land use changes.
clues.app_title: Land use guide on the app

clues.clue: The LPC protects historic buildings and neighborhoods by designating them as this.
clues.reveal: Landmarks. The Landmarks Preservation Commission (LPC) designates individual landmarks and historic districts.
clues.src_title: New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission

clues.clue: The NYPD and FDNY are the city's two largest agencies of this kind, handling crime and fire.
clues.reveal: Emergency. The NYPD and FDNY are the city's primary public safety and emergency response agencies.

clues.clue: Residents report potholes, noise, and broken signals to the city through this 3-digit hotline and app.
clues.reveal: 311. The city's non-emergency hotline and app routes service complaints to the right agency.

clues.clue: This state authority, not a city agency, runs the subways, buses, and commuter rails by its three-letter name.
clues.reveal: MTA. The Metropolitan Transportation Authority is a state authority that runs the subway, buses, and commuter rail.

clues.clue: New York City has 59 of these local bodies, like CB6, that advise on land use and budget priorities.
clues.reveal: Community Boards. The city's 59 community boards are the most local layer of government, advising on land use, budget, and services.
clues.src_title: Community boards of New York City

clues.clue: Each community board can have up to 50 of these unpaid appointed volunteers.
clues.reveal: Members. Community boards have up to 50 unpaid members, appointed by the borough president, half on the council member's recommendation.
clues.src_title: Community boards of New York City

clues.clue: Each board hires one paid professional with this title to run its office, like Mike Racioppo at CB6.
clues.reveal: District Manager. Each community board hires a District Manager to run its office and field constituent concerns.
clues.src_title: Community boards of New York City
